templates.subtopic: Cubic graphs
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B7 Non-linear graphs · S4 Cubic graphs
templates.text: For $y = x^3$, what happens to $y$ when $x$ is negative? Describe the shape of the graph.
templates.answer: $y$ is negative for negative $x$ ([[-k * k * k]] when $x = -[[k]]$); the graph rises from bottom left to top right through the origin with a flat point at the origin

templates.subtopic: Cubic graphs
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B7 Non-linear graphs · S4 Cubic graphs
templates.text: Complete the table for $y = x^3 - [[b]]x$ and write down the values of $x$ in the table where $y = 0$. Is the graph symmetrical about the origin? (4 marks)
templates.answer: $y = 0$ when $x = 0$ [[b == 1|if: and x = ±1/ ]][[b == 4|if: and x = ±2/ ]][[b == 9|if: and x = ±3/ ]]; yes, it has rotational symmetry about the origin

templates.subtopic: Estimate the gradient of a curve at a given point
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B7 Non-linear graphs · S6 Estimate the gradient of a curve at a given point
templates.text: For $y = x^2$, the gradient at $x = [[k]]$ is [[2 * k]]. A student draws a chord from $x = [[k]]$ to $x = [[k + 2]]$. Work out the gradient of the chord and compare it with the gradient of the tangent. (3 marks)
templates.answer: Chord gradient [[((k + 2) * (k + 2) - k * k) / 2]]; tangent gradient [[2 * k]]; the chord is steeper because it is over a bigger interval
